doc.title: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey Interview, 1959-03-15
doc.interviewee: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey

title: Joe Johnson, Johnny Brown and the trumpeter who called himself PVDQ Ned
summary: They try to recall early players including Joe Johnson and a trumpeter nicknamed Ned who played with Buddy.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Oh, we had a whole lot of musicians around here. We had a follow-up, he used to play... Johnny Browns? Johnny Browns would play violin. And he played clarinet after? Yeah. And you don't remember Stanley, do you? He used to play trombone for him?
Well, he used to talk about Joe Johnson.
I don't know if everybody ever mentioned about Joe Johnson. Joe Johnson. He's a trumpet player.
I've heard of him, don't know much about him. He played on front of him. No.
Well I didn't know, I hear him talk about it. My cousin used to play with him, he's from Carlton. Yeah, Joe, I saw a trumpet player.
And I see him talking about a trumpet player called Ned.
What was his name, Ned what? He used to play with Ned.
He used to play with Ned.
He used to play with Ned.

He used to play with Ned. He used to play with Ned. He used to play with Ned. He used to play with Ned. He was like a little mule on the face. Ned, yeah. He was like a little mule. Like a little jackass. Had a strong lip. Yeah, you knew him, man. I knew his son. I met his first class musician.
He was? Yeah, he was so Ned. He played with Buddy too.
He did? He played with Buddy Ball then too.
I know you got to do that by Buddy Johnson and Jack. Yeah, he was strong. Do you know Ned's name, is that his last name? P-V-D-Q Ned. I think that is right. P-V-D-Q Ned. What?
See what? P-V-D-Q Ned. P-V-D-Q Ned. P-V-D-Q Ned.
P-V-D-Q Ned. He called himself P-V-D-Q Ned. Oh, that's what he called himself. I think that was his... I think... I don't know if... I knew his boy. I don't remember my name Ned. Yeah.

Maybe Ned was his last name. I think it was. I think it was. Because he had a boy working at the Klobel and Derrick. When I was in the saloon business, he used to come in there and I used to give him credit. I can't remember the name.
